name: Baradin Bay
summary: Baradin Bay's reefs and wrecks make every crossing perilous. The waters lie between Khaz Modan, the Wetlands, the Arathi Highlands, and southern Lordaeron. During the Second War, Kul Tiras patrolled the bay with a powerful navy.

sections.title: A Strategic Waterway
sections.body: Baradin Bay joins the harbors of the Eastern Kingdoms. Menethil Harbor stands on the Wetlands shore, while Southshore lies in the Hillsbrad Foothills. Sandbanks and jagged shoals hide beneath the water. Murlocs, crocolisks, and deep-sea sharks make the passage more dangerous.

sections.title: Graveyard of the Fleets
sections.body: Kul Tiras and the Horde fought across Baradin Bay during the Second War. Along the Wetlands coast, the broken hulls of the Kul Tiran Third Fleet lie half-submerged. They are known as the Lost Fleet. Other ships sank at Drowned Reef. Hostile spirits, salvagers, and sea beasts haunt the waters around the ruined ships.

faq.q: What major ports are located along Baradin Bay?
faq.answer: Menethil Harbor in the Wetlands and Southshore in the Hillsbrad Foothills are the bay's chief ports. They sustain naval travel across the sea.

faq.q: Why are there so many shipwrecks along the bay's coast?
faq.answer: The wrecks along the Wetlands shore are the remains of the Kul Tiras Third Fleet, destroyed during the Second War. Other ships sank on Drowned Reef off the Arathi coast.

faq.q: What threats can be found in the waters of Baradin Bay?
aliases: is it safe to swim in baradin bay
faq.answer: Murlocs and swamp crocolisks threaten the shallows. Deeper waters hold predatory crabs, sharks, and restless spirits of drowned sailors.
Baradin Bay borders northwestern Dun Morogh, the Wetlands, the Arathi Highlands, southern Hillsbrad, and Gilneas.

angles.text: For the Alliance, Baradin Bay links operations in Khaz Modan with outposts in Arathi and Hillsbrad. Naval hazards and wreckage make every crossing risky.
As a human, especially one tracing your lineage to Kul Tiras or Lordaeron, you stand on solemn ground. Second War sailors rest beneath these waves.
